title: Fire: An Optimization Approach for Fast Interpretable Rule Extraction

problem.claim: Tree ensembles can produce many decision rules, creating a need to extract a small, useful, and practitioner-examinable rule collection.

gap.claim: Off-the-shelf solvers face challenges from the scale and non-convexity of the optimization problems involved in sparse, interpretable rule extraction.

contributions.claim: FIRE is an optimization-based framework for extracting sparse representative subsets of decision rules from tree ensembles.
FIRE uses fusion regularization to encourage selected rules to share common antecedents and a non-convex sparsity-inducing penalty to aggressively select rules.
FIRE includes a specialized solver based on block coordinate descent principles to address the scale and non-convexity of its optimization problems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The specialized solver performs up to 40x faster than existing solvers.
In the authors' experiments, FIRE outperforms state-of-the-art rule ensemble algorithms at building sparse rule sets.
In the authors' experiments, FIRE can deliver more interpretable models compared to existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper presents FIRE for extracting a small, useful collection of decision rules from tree ensembles.
FIRE selects sparse representative rules and encourages them to share common antecedents.
The framework combines fusion regularization with a non-convex sparsity-inducing penalty.
Because the optimization problems challenge off-the-shelf solvers, the authors develop a specialized block-coordinate-descent-based solver.
The authors report faster solving and improved sparse-rule and interpretability outcomes relative to existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Encouraging selected rules to share common antecedents is presented as a way to enhance interpretability.

interpretation.claim: Interpretability can be improved by structuring a sparse model so that its components reuse understandable conditions.

application.claim: When selecting human-facing rules, consider regularizing for shared structure in addition to sparsity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether shared antecedents improve interpretability across domains or user groups.

source_observation.claim: A specialized solver is reported to perform up to 40x faster than existing solvers.

interpretation.claim: Exploiting optimization problem structure may be important when model-selection objectives are large and non-convex.

application.claim: For structured non-convex selection problems, investigate specialized optimization algorithms rather than relying only on general-purpose solvers.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the benchmark conditions underlying the reported speedup.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The solver algorithm and optimization formulation are not described in detail.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported performance or interpretability results.
